_doc: Units that MUST keep running, and how long silence from each is tolerable.
Everything the estate built this month is a detector; nothing detected a detector dying. If
logscan.timer, freshness.timer or incident-digest.timer stopped, the estate would go completely
silent and look healthy — the queue would be empty, the digest would not post, and both are
indistinguishable from a good week. The digest even keeps a `quiet_runs` counter for exactly
this distinction and nothing read it.
max_hours is the longest gap that is NORMAL for that unit, with slack. Set it from the timer's
own cadence, not from hope: a unit that runs hourly and is silent for three hours is broken; one
that runs nightly is not late until well past its next window. loop@analyst is the exception -
its timer is 07..23, so an overnight gap of ~8 h is correct and 12 is the real bar.
This list is deliberately short. A watchdog that names forty units becomes a second incident
queue nobody reads; these are the ones whose silence would hide everything else.

units.why: the error-shaped-log scanner; its silence hides every other service's failures
the data-lane checker; its silence hides a dead lane
the only thing that speaks to the operator unprompted
the investigation record's only second copy
runs every 2 min; it is the estate's pulse and the publisher of every feed
uncommitted data is data one disk failure from gone
ring data; the vendor window is finite
the bank serves a ROLLING 90-day window - a stopped fetcher loses nights permanently
the standing investigator; timer is 07..23 so an overnight gap is normal
